description:
The layer-1 prototype needs a typed, user-created relation between research
nodes. Rust's `KnowledgeGraph.EdgeKind` today exposes only Classification,
WikiLink and Cites, so there is no canonical persistence API for a relation a
user draws by hand. The prototype works around this with
`kovan_relations.py`, a JSON shadow store under `.kovan/` that the README
states in so many words is NOT the proposed final format.

Model the prototype argues for:

  pub enum RelationKind {
      RelatedTo, Supports, Contradicts, DerivedFrom,
      UsesDataFrom, Validates, VerifiedAgainst, Implements,
  }

  pub struct UserRelation {
      pub id: String,
      pub source: NodeId,
      pub target: NodeId,
      pub kind: RelationKind,
  }

Operations:
  connections(node)
  add_connection(source, target, kind)
  edit_connection(id, target?, kind?)
  delete_connection(id)

HARD CONSTRAINT (op-9vo6 north star): user relations are authored knowledge,
not derived state, so they must be persisted in tracked human-readable files
(the artifact's fenced TOML or the paper's kovan.toml), never only in
`.kovan/`. `rm -rf .kovan` must not lose a single user-drawn connection.
Decide and record the on-disk shape before writing the API -- that decision is
the deliverable here as much as the code.

Design rules that apply: enum dispatch, no trait objects/Box/lifetimes.

Reference: collaboration/kovan-issue-35-prototypes/layer1-connections/
title: kovan: canonical UserRelation/RelationKind model + connection CRUD in Rust (replaces the prototype .kovan JSON shadow store)

description:
New crate crates/htgr-sim-web/ with crate-type=[cdylib,rlib]; hello-world eframe app; trunk serve; confirm WebGPU works with a WebGL fallback in BOTH Firefox and Chromium.

Deliberately first and deliberately trivial: doing this before any physics means a toolchain failure can never be mistaken for a physics failure. GH #39 Phase 0.

Acceptance: a blank egui window renders in two browsers from a static server.
title: Phase 0: prove the wasm toolchain before touching physics

description:
Two new capabilities plus a harness.

  * SIX-FACTOR FORMULA from the existing tally machinery. Needs a tally set resolving absorption/production by energy group and region.
  * RING RPT geometry construction alongside the existing explicit-TRISO path, so both run and compare inside the crate.
  * comparison harness: same case through both codes, per-quantity differences reported WITH uncertainties.

DO NOT TUNE THE RUST TO MATCH OPENMC. If they disagree that is the finding; record it.

Worth stating what is actually at stake: outram-mc-libs' declared maturity bar is k-eff within 500 pcm of ICSBEP Godiva, and the roster's own note says that figure 'is set at what it achieves today rather than at what criticality work should eventually demand'. Godiva is a bare HEU sphere and says nothing about double heterogeneity. So this exercise is a real test of whether 500 pcm survives on a TRISO pebble — and a worse number would be a legitimate, publishable finding, not a failure to hide.

Reuse, do not reinvent: run_keff_delta already implements Woodcock tracking for exactly this class of medium.
title: Phase 2: six-factor formula + ring RPT in outram-mc-libs

description: GitHub issue #30 comment 5384356411 opens with 'a feature where I can select text' -- distinct from drawing a region box. kopitiam_pdf::mupdf exposes page_to_stext(doc, page_index, StextOptions) -> StextPage with real per-line/per-char device-space bboxes (points, not pixels -- scale by RENDER_DPI/72.0 to match the reader's rasterized texture-pixel space). Scope: a 'Select text' tool that, on drag, selects the StextLines whose bbox intersects the drag rect, concatenates their text, and offers copy-to-clipboard / save-as-annotation. Not glyph-level character selection (line-granularity only) -- flagged as a deliberate scope cut unless line-granularity proves too coarse in practice.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Select text" tool alongside "Select"/"Draw box", using `kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::page_to_stext` (MuPDF's structured-text model, real per-line device-space bboxes -- not OCR, not pixel-region annotation).
- New free function `select_text_in_rect(page, scale, min, max) -> String`: concatenates the text of every StextLine whose bbox (converted from PDF points to this panel's texture-pixel space by `RENDER_DPI/72.0`, the same scale `rasterize_page` itself applies) intersects the drag rect. Line granularity, not character/glyph granularity -- documented as a deliberate scope cut in the module doc.
- `stext_for_page` caches the current page's `StextPage` (re-extracted on page change only, not kept for every page -- a full-res StextPage is a lot more data per page than a thumbnail texture).
- `text_selection_panel`: shows the last selection with Copy-to-clipboard and "Save as annotation" (folds the selection into the same `annotations` markdown section op-96am's hand-typed notes use).
- 4 new unit tests for `select_text_in_rect` against a hand-built `StextPage` fixture (intersection filtering, the DPI-scale conversion specifically, multi-line join, no-intersection case) -- exercises the real kopitiam_pdf types, not a mock.

Known limitation, disclosed rather than silently assumed away: the device-space-to-pixel-space conversion assumes the page has no rotation quirk beyond what `page_to_stext`'s own `page_mediabox` already handles internally -- not independently verified against `rasterize_page`'s own `page_is_quarter_turned` swap for a rotated page, since no rotated-page test fixture was available in this pass. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming full verification; worth a real-PDF smoke test with a rotated page if that turns out to matter in practice.

cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). cargo test --release: 191 kovan lib tests passing (8 new in pdf_reader alone this round). cargo doc --no-deps: no new warnings. Not committed yet.

title: kovan-literature/kovan: real PDF text selection via kopitiam_pdf structured text (StextPage), not just box-region annotation
